===PAGE page_0073===
Japanese From Zero! – Lesson 3 – Possession 73

Remember that the answer must follow the same pattern as the question, and therefore the
answer must also use が as the topic/subject marker.

Example Conversations
1. A: Dore が ＜ruma desu か。	Which one is a car?
   B: Sore が ＜ruma desu.	That's a car.

2. A: Dare が Tanaか san desu か。	Who/which is Tanaka?
   B: Tanaか san が tomodachi desu.	Tanaka is a friend.

Making words possessive with the particle no
It is easy to convert words into their possessive form by adding no after them.

Examples
mine	watashi no
mine	boく no
yours	anata no
hers	kaのjo no
his	kaれ no
whose	dare no

No also acts like the possessive 's in English when it follows a person's name and other
words.

Examples
Akiko's	あきこ no
Jeff's	Jeffu no
Mr. Tanaka's	Tanaか san no
Father's	おtoう san no
Mother's	おかあ san no
Grandfather's	おjiい san no
Grandmother's	おbaあ san no

===PAGE page_0074===
JapaneseFromZero.com 74

Using this concept in conversation is easy. If someone asks, こre wa dare no desu か
(Whose is this?) as they hold an object in their hand, you can use any of the following
answers:

Examples Answers
1. Watashi no desu.	It's mine.
2. Anata no desu.	It's yours.
3. Tanaか san no desu.	It's Mr. Tanaka's.
4. Kaのjo no desu.	It's hers.
5. おbaあ san no desu.	It's grandmother's.
6. Kaれ no desu.	It's his.
7. おかあ san no desu.	It's mother's.

Showing possession of objects using no
In the prior grammar section, you learned that the particle no is used to change words into
their possessive form. The possessive form can be used by itself or followed by another
word to show ownership. Try thinking of no as the glue the holds nouns together. You add
objects after the possessive form as follows:

Tanaka	's	car	it is
Tanaかsan no ＜ruma desu.	It is Tanaka's car.

Examples
my dog	watashi no iぬ nu
your mother	anata no おかあ san
her cat	kaのjo no neこ
his dog	kaれ no iぬ nu
father's pen	おtoう san no pen

The particle no is not limited to linking only two items. It can be used to further clarify the
object or item being discussed.

Examples
anata no kaのjo no namaえ	your girlfriend's name
おかあ san no neこ no namaえ	mother's cat's name

===PAGE page_0075===
Japanese From Zero! – Lesson 3 – Possession 75

Now let's put your new knowledge of no into practice. These sentences may appear long at
first, but they're using the simple grammar you've learned already.

Example Sentences
1. Anata no kaのjo no namaえ wa nan desu か。
What is your girlfriend's name?

2. Tanaか san no おかあ san wa nansai desu か。
How old is Tanaka san's mother?

3. Koばyashi san no おtoう san wa dare desu か。
Who is Kobayashi san's father?

3 Q&A しつもん と こたえ E→J

1. Who is it?	Dare desu か。
It's me.	Watashi desu.
It's Hideko.	Hideこ desu.
It's Mom.	おかあ san desu.

2. Whose car is it?	Dare no ＜ruma desu か。
It's my car.	Watashi no ＜ruma desu.
It's mine.	Watashi no desu.
It's Mr. Takada's car.	Taかda san no ＜ruma desu.
I don't know.	Waか rimasen.

3. Which one is your rabbit?	Docchi が anata no うsaぎ desu か。
That one over there is my rabbit.	あcchi が watashi no うsaぎ desu.
It's that one.	Socchi desu.

4. Is this your car?	こre wa anata no ＜ruma desu か。
Yes, it is.	Haい, soう desu.
No, it's my friend's car.	いいえ、tomodachi no ＜ruma desu.
No, it's her car.	いいえ、kaのjo no ＜ruma desu.
No, it's hers.	いいえ、kaのjo no desu.

5. Which one is your bird?	Anata no tori wa dore desu か。
My bird is that one.	Boく no tori wa sore desu.

===PAGE page_0076===
JapaneseFromZero.com 76

3 Q&A しつもん と こたえ J→E

1. Anata no neこ wa dore desu か。	Which one is your cat?
Watashi no neこ wa sore desu.	My cat is that one.
Watashi no neこ wa あre desu.	My cat is that one over there.

2. おかあ san no namaえ wa nan desu か。	What is (your) mother's name?
Maria desu.	It's Maria.
Yoshiこ desu.	It's Yoshiko.

3. Sore wa kaのjo no taoru desu か。	Is that her towel?
いいえ、kaれ no taoru desu.	No, it's his towel.
いいえ、Mamiこ san no taoru desu.	No, it's Mamiko's towel.

4. Anata no tomodachi no iぬ nu no	What is your friend's dog's name?
namaえ wa nan desu か。
Iぬ nu no namaえ wa Pochi desu.	The dog's name is Pochi.
Waか rimasen.	I don't know.

3 Reading Comprehension どっかい

Read the sentences below. Use the information to answer the reading comprehension
questions later in this lesson.

① Watashi no namaえ wa Honda desu.
② Sanjuうご saい desu.
③ Watashi no kaのjo no namaえ wa Terada desu.
④ Kaのjo wa nijuうきゅう saい desu.

===PAGE page_0077===
Japanese From Zero! – Lesson 3 – Hiragana さしすせそ 77

Hiragana さしすせそ

さ New Hiragana あたらしいう ひらがな

Make sure you learn the correct stroke order since correct stroke order will mean neater
characters when writing quickly.

SA	SHI	SU	SE	SO
さ	し	す	せ	そ

ZA	JI	ZU	ZE	ZO
ざ	じ	ず	ぜ	ぞ

さ Various Styles スタイル

Look at the various possible styles for the hiragana in this lesson. Write each symbol as neatly
as you can, then compare to the different versions below.

さしすせそ	さしすせそ	さしすせそ	さしすせそ	さしすせそ
ざじずぜぞ	ざじずぜぞ	ざじずぜぞ	ざじずぜぞ	ざじずぜぞ
